messages.content: What is the freezing point point of water at a pressure of 10 kPa?

function.name: thermodynamics_calculate_boiling_point

message.content:
At a pressure of **10 kPa** (≈ 0.1 atm) water’s freezing (melting) point is **about –2 °C**.  
This follows from the water phase diagram: as pressure drops below atmospheric, the solid–liquid equilibrium line slopes downward, so the temperature at which ice melts (or water freezes) falls. At 10 kPa the equilibrium temperature is roughly –2 °C (≈ −3.6 °F).
